titles.name: Name
offline: Connect to the radio to see this.
privacy.shareHint: Everyone who hears its advert sees it on their map.
privacy.nameNote: Everyone hears its name in every advert; it cannot be hidden.
privacy.closed: The radio answers nobody who asks.
trusted.note: They get what Privacy opens to trusted contacts.
remote.warn: They may do all you can in the radio's console: reboot it and turn it off, change its name, PIN and frequency, read its Wi-Fi password.
remote.askBody: {name} will be able to reboot {radio} over the air and turn it off, change its name, PIN and frequency, and read its Wi-Fi password.
remote.nobodyYet: People from your contacts show here.
trusted.nobodyYet: No people among the contacts yet.
position.none: This device would not say where it is
name.name: Name
name.nameHint: Other radios see it in adverts and before your channel messages.
position.latitudeHint: Or paste both, as a map copies them: 55.75580, 37.61730.
position.useDeviceGps: The radio's GPS puts its own in place once it picks up satellites.
position.followHint: The radio gets a new position when the phone has moved more than 50 m. At most once in 5 minutes, while the app is open.
position.followRough: The phone knows its place only roughly (±{accuracy} m), so the radio stays put.
position.followGps: The radio has its own GPS and takes its position from it.
position.followDenied: Following the phone is off: no access to its location.
position.mapHint: Or on the map: hold a spot, then “Put this radio here”.
position.mapHintMouse: Or on the map: right-click a spot, then “Put this radio here”.
privacy.shareFollowHint: Others see on their map where you are, with the next advert.
locate.denied: No access to location. You can allow it for Ommesh in the phone's settings.
locate.off: Location is turned off on this phone.
locate.timeout: The phone could not find where it is. Try under the open sky.
frequency.repeatOn: The radio will pass on other people's messages.
frequency.repeatOff: The radio will stop passing on other people's messages.
frequency.hashLonger: Repeaters on firmware before 1.14 drop messages with a hash of {size}.
frequency.hashShorter: Messages will pass every repeater again.
region.title: Region
region.name: Name
region.note: The repeaters' owners choose the name. Ask people nearby, or ask the repeaters.
region.invalid: Only lower-case Latin letters, digits and hyphens, up to 30.
region.listening: Looking for repeaters that hear the radio
region.unscopedHint: Only through repeaters that let such messages through
region.noneFound: None of them is set to a region.
region.nobodyNear: No repeater nearby heard the radio.
search.nothing: Nothing found. Chats and nodes are searched in their own sections.
search.words.name: callsign nickname name
search.words.preset: eu us anz oms omsk preset
search.words.readings: battery charge voltage sensors temperature telemetry
search.words.quiet: quiet silence night sleep mute dnd do not disturb
search.words.lookalikes: latin cyrillic letters lookalikes cyr2lat handwriting
search.words.readCyrillic: latin cyrillic letters lookalikes cyr2lat read
search.words.backup: backup copy move transfer new radio restore contacts
search.words.wifi: wifi wi-fi network password tcp ip
search.words.sharedSettings: sync same alike phone computer read
search.words.off: turn off power off shut down
search.words.report: report bug problem error idea issue github send
frequency.confirmBody: Radios still on the old settings stop hearing this one until they change too.
battery.lto2sHint: 3.6–5.6 V · two titanate cells in series
console.radioWarn: The radio moves to these settings from its next reboot and may drop off your mesh.
advanced.setClock: Set the radio's clock from this device
advanced.clockAhead: The radio's clock runs {seconds} s ahead and cannot go back
notifications.blocked: Notifications are turned off for this app in the system's settings
notifications.ownDesktopWindows: {app} draws them in a corner of the screen, also while its window is in the tray. Windows keeps none of them.
notifications.ownDesktop: {app} draws them in a corner of the screen, also while its window is in the tray. The system keeps none of them.
notifications.ownPhone: While {app} is open, a banner slides in at the top. With it closed, the phone shows them as before.
notifications.ownTab: While this tab is on screen, a banner slides in at the top. Hidden, the browser shows them as before.
notifications.systemDesktopWindows: Windows draws them and keeps them in its notification centre.
notifications.systemDesktop: The system draws them and keeps them in its notification centre.
notifications.systemPhone: The phone's own banners, also while {app} is open.
notifications.chatsAll: Every message in a chat you are not looking at.
notifications.nodesPeople: A person's radio heard for the first time. Not repeaters, rooms or sensors.
notifications.nodesAll: Any node heard for the first time.
notifications.popupsNote: A chat can have its own setting on its page. A tap on a notification opens the chat or the node.
notifications.settingsPhoneHint: Vibration, the lock screen, quiet hours.
notifications.settingsHint: Banners, the lock screen, Do not disturb.
notifications.settingsFailed: Could not open the system's settings
quiet.statusAlways: Quiet until you turn it off
quiet.favouritesHint: People with a star in the contacts, with the sound as usual.
quiet.mentionsHint: Someone writes @[{name}] in a channel or a room.
quiet.note: The rest comes without a sound and without popping up, and waits among the system's notifications. New nodes are not announced. Unread chats show as usual.
corner.label: Corner
sound.desktop: Plays with every notice, the app's own and the system's, except in a full-screen app, a presentation or Do not disturb.
sound.android: Plays with every notice. Silent mode and Do not disturb still keep it quiet. A new sound makes the notification channels anew, so a sound picked for one in Android's settings gives way to this one.
sound.ios: Plays with every notice. Silent mode and Do not disturb still keep it quiet.
sound.web: Plays with the banner in this tab. The browser's own notices ring with the system's sound.
signals.chirpHint: A LoRa preamble, slowed down: two up, one down.
signals.hopHint: Three hops up the mesh, the last one relayed.
messages.openAtUnreadHint: A chat with new messages opens where they begin, not at the latest one.
messages.lookalikesHint: а е о р с х and А В Е К М Н О Р С Т Х go out as their Latin twins: they look the same and take one byte instead of two, so about a fifth more text fits.
messages.nearHint: Also у → y, ё → e, З → 3, Ь → b. ё loses its dots.
messages.cursiveHint: Also т → m, п → n, и → u. In print the difference shows.
messages.readCyrillicHint: Latin twins among Cyrillic letters are shown as Cyrillic: Bcmpeчa y мocma → Встреча у моста.
messages.previewsTapHint: A mark follows each link: tap it for the preview, tap again to fold it.
messages.previewsAutoHint: A preview appears by itself when its message is on screen.
messages.previewsNote: Previews are made by the Ommesh server, preview.cm4ker.ru: it visits the link, so the site sees the server, never your device. The server gets only the link, keeps the preview for a day and keeps no log of links. Previews never go on air.
messages.triesNote: Chats and rooms. A message the other side has not acknowledged goes again on its own: the first try by the route, the rest flood. Channels keep their own Keep trying.
messages.sentOnce: Sent once. With no acknowledgement, sending again is up to you.

messages.triesMinute.one: {count} try within a minute, then the message turns red.
messages.triesMinute.other: {count} tries within a minute, then the message turns red.

messages.triesOver.one: {count} try over ~{minutes} min, then the message turns red.
messages.triesOver.other: {count} tries over ~{minutes} min, then the message turns red.

messages.routesNote: Chats and rooms. A route learned this long ago is dropped, and the next message floods to find a fresh one. A route set by hand stays. A contact can set its own on its Route page.
messages.routesOffline: Kept per radio: connect to change it.
messages.routesNodesHint: The next request floods once, and its answer brings a fresh route.
history.bringInHint: An Ommesh file or the MeshCore app's database
history.note: The file holds your private messages and channel keys: keep it as you would a password. Node passwords are not in it.
history.title: Bring in this history?
history.body: Messages join this radio's chats, and one already here is not added twice. Contacts the radio does not hold go to Removed, to be put back from there.

history.leftChannel.one: {name}, {count} message, as the radio has no such channel
history.leftChannel.other: {name}, {count} messages, as the radio has no such channel

history.toRemoved.one: {count} contact the radio does not hold is in Removed.
history.toRemoved.other: {count} contacts the radio does not hold are in Removed.

history.nothing: There is nothing in this file to bring in.
history.notHistory: This is neither an Ommesh history file nor a database the MeshCore app exported.
history.newer: A newer Ommesh saved this file. Update the app to bring it in.
history.badField: This file does not follow the history format at {path}.
history.otherRadio: This history belongs to another radio ({key}…). Connect to that one to bring it in.
backup.hasNoKey: Name and settings, without the key
backup.restoreHint: Onto this radio, from a copy's file
backup.note: The file holds {name}'s private key and your direct messages. Whoever has it can write as {name}: keep it like a password. Node passwords are not in it.
backup.historyHint: On its own, and from the MeshCore app
backup.savedKeyless: Saved without the key: this radio's firmware does not give it out. Another radio restored from this copy stays a node of its own.
backup.resetUnsaved: There is no copy of {name} yet.
backup.notBackup: This is not a copy of a radio. Ommesh saves one under Copy and move.
backup.newer: A newer Ommesh saved this copy. Update the app to restore it.
backup.badField: This copy does not follow its format at {path}.
backup.done: The copy is on the radio
backup.doneFull: The radio filled up: the other contacts are in Removed.
backup.blank: A new radio with nothing on it. Moving from another?
backup.moved: {name} moved to another radio {when}. This one has the same key: reset it, so that the two do not get in each other's way.
restore.pickNote: A copy is saved on the old radio, under Settings › Copy and move.
restore.sameHint: Its key stays, the rest comes back
restore.noKeyHint: The radio stays {name}, a node of its own

restore.contactsOver.one: {count} will not fit: favourites and those you wrote with go first, the rest wait in Removed
restore.contactsOver.other: {count} will not fit: favourites and those you wrote with go first, the rest wait in Removed

restore.contactsRoom: With favourites and routes; the radio holds {count}
restore.messagesKey: Only with the key: they are its chats
restore.appHint: Pins, notifications, routes set by hand
restore.oldRadio: Then switch the old {name} off or reset it: two radios with one key get in each other's way.
restore.refusedTitle: This radio does not take another key
restore.refusedBody: Its firmware does not let a key be written. Nothing has been written yet.
restore.refusedRest: The rest can come back: channels, contacts, settings. But the radio stays {name}, a new node: friends will have to add it again, and {old}'s chats stay in the app under the old key.
restore.keepNear: Keep the radio close and the app open. If the link drops, tap Restore again: what is written already is skipped.
appearance.themeHint: One Light or One Dark, as the system is set
appearance.sampleIn: Anyone hearing me from the valley?
appearance.largeEmojiHint: A message of only emoji, up to three, is drawn large, without a bubble.
background.chatNote: A chat can have its own: on its page, Background.
about.note: A companion for MeshCore radios. Messages stay on this device; the radio keeps only what has not been read yet.
about.stoppedNote: When and why Android stopped the app, or the page inside it, as Android says. Worth a screenshot when the app keeps closing.
about.report: Report a problem or an idea
report.note: It goes to GitHub as an open issue, which anyone can read. You need no account there.
report.placeholder: Say what you did, what you expected and what happened instead.
report.attach: Add the log and the radio's setup
report.attachHint: The app's and the radio's versions, the radio's settings and the latest events. Not the radio's name, key, position or PIN, and no messages.
report.sentNote: Thank you. Follow the issue on GitHub: questions about it are asked there.
report.tooMany: Too many reports from here just now. Try again in an hour, or copy it and send it another way.
report.offline: The server could not be reached. Check the internet, or copy the report and send it another way.
report.refused: The server did not take the report. Copy it and send it another way.
people.note: The people who write Ommesh and the people who take it out on real radios and report what they find.
connection.minimisedConnects: Opens minimised and connects to the radio.
connection.shareNote: A computer nearby connects to this phone over Bluetooth, as if it were the radio, and uses the radio through it, with the phone locked too. Both can use the radio at once, and each gets every message.
connection.sharedSettingsHint: Theme, backgrounds, sounds and each chat's settings stay the same on the phone and the computer. What is read is always shared.
connection.anotherNote: For one more radio. Each window keeps its own radio and opens with it next time.
connection.disconnectNote: Both lead to the connect screen, where another radio can be picked.
power.note: A factory reset erases every contact, channel and setting on the radio, and its identity with them. Deleting history leaves the radio untouched.
power.forget: Delete the history on this device
power.rebootBody: The link drops and comes back when the radio is up.
power.resetBody: Every contact, channel and setting on the radio is erased, and its identity with them: it becomes a new node with a new key. This cannot be undone.
power.forgetBody: Every message this device has kept for this radio is deleted. The radio itself is untouched.
power.offBody: {name} leaves the mesh and this app. Only the button on the radio itself turns it on again.
home.title: Settings
home.floodHint: A flood every repeater passes on. Costs airtime.
home.resync: Read everything from the radio again
home.release: Release to read from the radio
home.pull: Pull to read from the radio
air.note: Listening only: nothing is sent. What the radio could not decode is not here.
log.recordHint: Hex of what crosses the link, for reading the protocol.
sensors.read: Read {time}, from the radio, not over the air. Read again every half minute while open.
sensors.who: Who may ask for these readings
key.save: Save the key to a file
key.closed: This radio's firmware does not give out its key
key.closedNote: That is how this radio's firmware was built. The usual MeshCore firmware gives the key out.
key.restoreHint: From a file, or pasted as text
key.pickHint: An Ommesh file, or text with the key
key.pasteHint: The private key, 128 hex digits, as the MeshCore app and the get prv.key command give it
key.pasteFailed: Could not take the text from the clipboard. Paste it into the field yourself.

key.short.one: {count} digit short: a private key has 128. It looks like only part of it was copied.
key.short.other: {count} digits short: a private key has 128. It looks like only part of it was copied.

key.notHex: A key has only the digits 0–9 and the letters a–f.
key.notKey: This file holds no radio key.
key.newer: A newer version of Ommesh saved this file. Update the app to read it.
key.shape: This is not a MeshCore radio key; the radio will not take it.
key.prefix: The radio will not take this key: the mesh keeps keys like it for itself.
key.same: This radio already has this key
key.hasChats: its chats are on this device
key.noChats: none of its chats are on this device
key.askBody: To the whole mesh the radio becomes the node with this key. The radio will reboot.
key.askBodyChats: To the whole mesh the radio is this node again, and its chats come back on this device. The radio will reboot.
key.askLoses: The current key, {name}'s, has never been saved and will be lost.
key.refused: This radio's firmware does not take a key
key.rebooting: Key written, the radio is rebooting
pin.randomHint: A radio with a screen shows a new one each time it starts. Without a screen, 123456.
pin.note: The PIN is asked for only at the first pairing: phones and computers paired already connect without it. Write your own PIN down for a radio without a screen: a forgotten one can be reset only over USB.
pin.askOwn: The new PIN is {pin}. It takes effect after the reboot, and the link comes back by itself.
pin.askRandom: A radio with a screen will show a new PIN each time it starts, one without a screen takes 123456. This takes effect after the reboot, and the link comes back by itself.
pin.rebooting: PIN saved, the radio is rebooting
wifi.ssidLong: A network name is at most {max} characters
wifi.passwordLong: A password is at most {max} characters
wifi.saved: Saved. It works once the radio reboots
